_comment: Half-step coverage, run in EVERY language. docs/00 §7 records the same safety bug found in
two independent layers on the day docs/04 §2 changed Schedule from int to multiples of 0.5:
the comparator truncated with int(), so a prescribed HALF against a patient who heard ONE
scored as a match; and the extractor mapped the word 'half' to 0, so a prescribed ZERO
against a patient saying 'half' also scored as a match. Both are silent, both are a wrong
dose recorded as understood, and NEITHER WOULD EVER FIRE ON A WHOLE-NUMBER TEST CASE.
That is what this file is for. Every case below is a half-step, and `score.py halfstep`
additionally re-runs the whole set through two deliberately broken comparators — one that
truncates, one that reads 'half' as 0 — and FAILS if either of them survives the suite.
A suite that a known-broken comparator can pass is not a suite.
These are mechanical structures, not patient-facing strings, so they carry no
NEEDS-NATIVE-REVIEW tag. Where a case needs the patient's own word for a dose, it says
'@count_word:0.5' and the harness reads that word out of content/readback/<lang>.yaml at
run time — there is deliberately no second copy of that table to go stale (docs/00 §6).

render_cases.why: the commonest half in Indian practice — half a thyroid tablet before food
1.5 is a single suppletive word in all three languages and must never be built by concatenating 'one' and 'half'
a half in one slot and a whole in another, in one sentence — the two must not blur
half-steps are not only tablets; a syrup is counted in spoons and takes a different form noun and verb
Hindi's word for half agrees with the form noun (आधी गोली, आधा कैप्सूल); a masculine form must not take the feminine word

teachback_cases.why_wrong: prescribed half, patient repeats one — a DOUBLE DOSE. int() scores it a match
teachback_cases.catches: docs/00 §7 bug 1: int() truncation in the comparator

teachback_cases.why_wrong: prescribed nothing in the morning, patient says half — an EXTRA DOSE. 'half'->0 scores it a match
teachback_cases.catches: docs/00 §7 bug 2: the word 'half' parsed as 0 in the extractor

teachback_cases.why_wrong: prescribed one and a half, patient repeats one — a THIRD of the dose missing
teachback_cases.catches: a comparator that reads only the leading digit of '1.5'

teachback_cases.why_wrong: prescribed one, patient repeats one and a half — half a tablet too much, the same error the other way round
teachback_cases.catches: int() truncation, which rounds the heard 1.5 back down onto the prescribed 1

teachback_cases.why_wrong: NOT wrong — the patient says the half back correctly, in English. A comparator that flags this over-flags and every catch above is worthless
NOT wrong — the patient says the half back in their OWN language, in the very word the read-back spoke. Resolved from content/readback/<lang>.yaml at run time
teachback_cases.catches: a parser that understands only English, which would score a correct patient as not having answered

teachback_cases.why_wrong: NOT wrong — 1.5 repeated in the patient's own suppletive word (ஒன்றரை / ಒಂದೂವರೆ / डेढ़)
teachback_cases.catches: a parser that handles 0.5 but not the other half-steps

parse_cases.why: the §7 bug in one word: this must never be 0
must beat the bare 'half' inside it
the digit form, as the extractor normalises it
the only phrase that may be 0
the patient's own word for a half
the patient's own word for one and a half
